facts.fact: Ratoma commune's delegated civil status officer says the commune offices establish digital birth certificates on secure paper and that registration operations were continuing on 2 September 2026 despite a stockout of that paper.

Ratoma's civil status officer says the digital birth-certificate system used in the communes depends on a data centre formerly hosted at the Maison centrale, whose relocation disturbed the system while registrations continued (reported 2 September 2026).

Ratoma's civil status officer says the secure paper serves to establish digital birth certificates in all the communes of Guinea, and the article says several communes face the same stockout; no count of offices is given (reported 2 September 2026).

Printing of digital birth certificates had been halted for about two weeks by a stockout of secure paper, with resupply expected in about a week, according to Ratoma's civil status officer on 2 September 2026.

The relocation of the data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted the digital birth-certificate system, with engineers reinstalling it at a new site and expected to finish within the week, according to Ratoma's civil status officer on 2 September 2026.
Ratoma's civil status officer says an unnamed company in charge of the secure papers is the one reinstalling the data centre at new premises with its engineers (reported 2 September 2026).

systems.owner: an unnamed company in charge of the secure paper and the data centre
systems.tiers: commune civil status offices; the officer says all communes of Guinea

note: The document does not say in terms whether the digital certificate is made at first declaration of a birth or for an existing record; it says commune offices establish it and that registrations continue.
